messages:
Maya: heads up — I just finished onboarding model v3.2.0-int4 into staging and kicked off a mini-canary against a long-context slice (docs >4k tokens).
Raj: whats the exact slice definition and sample size?
Maya: long_seq = docs with >4000 tokens, use-case tags: doc-summary, email-digest. sample = 2k requests over 30m from recent production traffic.
Simon: quick smoke: latency p95 +40ms, cost per token down ~22% — good on perf.
Eva: quality flags: rouge-l avg down 0.8% on long_seq, hallucination-rate +1.9% (human-eval sampled). Short-context slices show slight positive lift.
Maya: hmm. global promote policy would have promoted, but long_seq is a clear regression.
Raj: do we have seqlen-aware gating today? I thought gates were global.
Maya: currently global. that's the problem. long-tail contexts need separate thresholds.
Simon: suggested quick fallback thresholds: per-slice rouge_drop <=1.0% and hallucination_increase <=1.0% for long_seq.
Eva: agree, and add an absolute hard auto-fallback if hallucination delta > 1.0% or rouge drop > 1.0% for any 15m window.
Maya: rolling back long_seq traffic to 0% and leaving short-slices at 5% for more signal collection.
Raj: proposed gate config snippet: 
```yaml
gates:
  promote:
    global:
      rouge_drop_pct: 0.5
      hallucination_inc_pct: 0.5
      latency_p95_ms: 30
    slices:
      long_seq:
        rouge_drop_pct: 1.0
        hallucination_inc_pct: 1.0
        latency_p95_ms: 50
fallback:
  auto: true
  cooldown_mins: 15
  traffic_shift_pct: -100
```
Simon: also add EWMA smoothing (alpha=0.2) on slice metrics to avoid reacting to single noisy batches.
Eva: plus tie each canary run to model-version tags and a run-id so we can trace individual evals back to samples.
Maya: I'll open a short runbook update: add seqlen-aware gate, EWMA smoothing, 15m grace window, and auto-fallback rules.
deploy-bot: Canary update: v3.2.0-int4 deployed -> short-slices 5%, long_seq 0% (rollback applied).
SRE-Alex: watching memory & KV-cache impact for long contexts; will alert on GPU mem > 85% or tail latency spike.
Raj: plan for next steps: run a 12h shadow compare only on long_seq with richer evals (human-review + hallucination classifier), then re-run with per-slice thresholds tightened.
Simon: I'll own the shadow compare and extend the eval harness to include hallucination source tagging.
Eva: I'll coordinate human sample labeling and add a small calibration set.
Maya: thanks — assigning follow-ups in the canary board. any objections to making seqlen-slice gating the default for future onboards?
Raj: no objections. makes sense given long-context risk vector.
Simon: +1. also consider automatic fallback to a larger-precision variant (v3.2.0-fp16) for long_seq if int4 fails.
Maya: good idea — fall back to compatible variant before full rollback where possible.
Eva: adding that to the runbook checklist. :thumbsup:
Maya: closing for now, will post the eval plots and a runbook PR when ready.
Simon: thanks, will post progress in this thread.
Maya: end
